_comment: A ratchet, not a target. Each number may only go DOWN, and the way to lower it is to fix the
code and write the smaller number here. Raising a number to make a check pass is the escape hatch
this file exists to catch, so it needs a reason in the commit message.
These are ratchets and not bans because the honest counts are too big to ban outright: real code
needs a cast at a JSON boundary and a best-effort teardown that must not throw. The bans that ARE
absolute live in tests/architectureBoundaries.test.ts, where the count is genuinely zero today.
Never read these numbers from this file: run npm run quality, which recomputes them, and
node scripts/quality.mjs --where, which says where each one is heaviest. The scan strips comments,
